फरीदाबाद। शुक्रवार सुबह से निकली तेज धूप ने लोगों की परेशानी बढ़ा दी। दिन चढ़ने के साथ गर्मी और उमस का असर बढ़ता गया। उमस अधिक होने के कारण लोग पसीने से तरबतर नजर आए। गर्मी से बचने के लिए लोगों ने दोपहर के समय घरों से निकलने से भी परहेज किया। शहरवासियों को अब बारिश का इंतजार है, ताकि गर्मी और उमस से राहत मिल सके।
शुक्रवार को सुबह से ही तेज धूप खिली रही। दोपहर के समय धूप का असर और बढ़ गया। गर्मी और उमस के कारण बाजारों और सड़कों पर भी सामान्य दिनों की अपेक्षा लोगों की आवाजाही कम दिखाई दी। जरूरी काम से बाहर निकले लोगों को भी गर्मी का सामना करना पड़ा। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार शुक्रवार को जिले में अधिकतम तापमान 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 29 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। मौसम में उमस रहने के कारण तापमान से अधिक गर्मी महसूस हुई। मौसम विभाग ने शनिवार को भी बारिश होने की संभावना जताई है। शनिवार को अधिकतम तापमान 37 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 28 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने की संभावना है। बारिश होने से तापमान में गिरावट के साथ लोगों को उमस और गर्मी से कुछ राहत मिल सकती है। शहरवासियों का कहना है कि पिछले कुछ दिनों से मौसम में गर्मी और उमस बनी हुई है। ऐसे में बारिश होने से लोगों को राहत मिलने की उम्मीद है। मौसम विभाग की बारिश की संभावना के चलते लोगों की नजर आसमान पर टिकी हुई है।

हिमाचल के चार जिलों में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट, कल से कमजोर पड़ेगा मानसून, धूप निकलने के साथ बढ़ेगा तापमान
मानसून की गतिविधियां कमजोर होने और धूप बढ़ने से प्रदेश के तापमान में दो से तीन डिग्री सेल्सियस तक बढ़ोतरी हो सकती है.
शिमला: हिमाचल प्रदेश में बारिश का दौर फिलहाल पूरी तरह खत्म नहीं हुआ है. शनिवार को प्रदेश के चार जिलों में भारी बारिश को लेकर यलो अलर्ट जारी किया गया है. वहीं, रविवार से मानसून की गतिविधियों में कमी आने का अनुमान है. अगले कुछ दिनों में बारिश कम होने के साथ धूप बढ़ेगी और तापमान में भी इजाफा हो सकता है. मौसम विभाग के अनुसार शनिवार को बिलासपुर, चंबा, कांगड़ा और मंडी में भारी बारिश की संभावना है. इन जिलों के कुछ हिस्सों में तेज बारिश के दौर देखने को मिल सकते हैं. प्रदेश के बाकी जिलों में भी मौसम पूरी तरह साफ रहने की उम्मीद नहीं है. कई जगह हल्की बारिश या बूंदाबांदी हो सकती है. इससे पहले शुक्रवार को कांगड़ा और हमीरपुर के कई इलाकों में बारिश हुई. वहीं, शिमला और मनाली में सुबह के समय हल्की बूंदाबांदी हुई.
कल से कमजोर पड़ेगा मानसून
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार रविवार से प्रदेश में बारिश की गतिविधियां कमजोर पड़ सकती हैं. इसके बाद अगले पांच दिनों तक ज्यादातर क्षेत्रों में मौसम अपेक्षाकृत साफ रहने की संभावना है. हालांकि, कुछ स्थानों पर हल्की बारिश हो सकती है. 27 अगस्त तक प्रदेश के अधिकांश हिस्सों में धूप खिलने का अनुमान है.
बारिश कम होते ही बढ़ेगा तापमान
मानसून की गतिविधियां कमजोर होने और धूप बढ़ने से प्रदेश के तापमान में दो से तीन डिग्री सेल्सियस तक बढ़ोतरी हो सकती है. प्रदेश के कई शहरों में अधिकतम तापमान पहले ही सामान्य से ऊपर दर्ज किया जा रहा है. शुक्रवार को ऊना में सबसे अधिक 33.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान दर्ज किया गया. इसके अलावा शिमला में 24.5°C, सुंदरनगर में 31.8°C, भुंतर में 33.0°C, कल्पा में 24.5°C, धर्मशाला में 29.0°C, नाहन में 27.8°C, केलांग में 22.7°C, सोलन में 29.0°C, मनाली में 25.2°C, कांगड़ा में 31.6°C, मंडी में 33.0°C, बिलासपुर में 33.0°C, चंबा में 30.7°C, जुब्बरहट्टी में 27.6°C और ताबो में 27.7°C.
इस मानसून सीजन में 8 फीसदी कम बारिश

शुक्रवार को 15 जिलों में बारिश का यलो अलर्ट जारी किया गया था, लेकिन ज्यादातर जिलों में मौसम साफ रहा। जिन इलाकों में बारिश हुई, वहां भी अधिकांश जगह बारिश हल्की रही। उपलब्ध मौसम आंकड़ों के अनुसार किशनगंज और अटरू में कुल 9 मिमी, भरतपुर के बयाना, उच्चैन और वैर में 6 मिमी तथा धौलपुर में 5 मिमी बारिश दर्ज हुई। कोटा के कानावास में 3 मिमी और उदयपुर के मावली में 1 मिमी बारिश हुई।
ट्रफ लाइन राजस्थान से दूर, इसलिए मानसून कमजोर
मौसम विशेषज्ञों के अनुसार मानसून की सक्रियता में ट्रफ लाइन की अहम भूमिका होती है। वर्तमान में मानसून ट्रफ उत्तर भारत की ओर खिसकी हुई है। यही वजह है कि राजस्थान में बारिश की गतिविधियां सीमित हो गई हैं। मौसम विभाग के राष्ट्रीय पूर्वानुमान में भी 20 से 22 अगस्त के दौरान पूर्वी राजस्थान में बारिश की संभावना जताई गई थी।
जयपुर में उमस बढ़ी, बारिश का इंतजार
राजधानी जयपुर में शुक्रवार को बारिश का अलर्ट होने के बावजूद ज्यादातर समय मौसम साफ रहा। हल्के बादल छाए रहे, लेकिन बारिश नहीं हुई। इसके कारण उमस बढ़ गई। जयपुर में शुक्रवार को अधिकतम तापमान 34.9 डिग्री और न्यूनतम 27.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। शनिवार को भी जयपुर में गरज-चमक के साथ छिटपुट बारिश की संभावना बनी हुई है।
कुल मिलाकर, राजस्थान में फिलहाल मानसून का सक्रिय दौर नहीं है। पूर्वी राजस्थान में शनिवार को कुछ राहत मिल सकती है, लेकिन 23 अगस्त के बाद बारिश की गतिविधियां फिर कम होने के आसार हैं। राजस्थान में 21 अगस्त तक बारिश की कमी 14.1 प्रतिशत तक पहुंच गई है।

Retail sales across Great Britain weakened last month despite the men’s football World Cup and record temperatures boosting the demand for food and drink.
The Office for National Statistics said the volume of goods sold in stores and online fell 0.5% in July. That is down from 0.7% rise in June – revised down from initial estimates of 1% – and a 1.3% rise in May.
Non-food stores took the biggest tumble, falling 1.3%, on the back of a drop in clothes shopping, after retailers brought forward cut-price sales into June while heatwaves in July resulted in more people staying home than hitting the high street.
Sandra Prince, the head of consumer at Lloyds, said: “Hotter days could have shifted footfall and spending online or towards retail parks. For retailers, as the summer peak slows down, attention is now turning to the opportunities the autumn could bring to keep consumers engaged.”
Demand for furniture also took a dive, with fewer households looking to change decor during the extreme heat, while department stores suffered because of a drop in available stock. Some retailers had warned of lengthier delivery times during recent heatwaves.
Food and drink sales were a rare bright spot, however, as hot and sunny weather and excitement around World Cup games boosted demand.
However, the gains could have been higher had it not been for pubs and sports bars – which count as hospitality rather than retail in official statistics – luring punters to their screens to watch big matches.
The British Beer & Pub Association said last month that late opening hours and England’s progress to the semi-finals gave a big boost to the industry, with pubs pouring an extra 30m pints than normal over the course of the tournament. That produced an extra £150m in added sales for its members.
Jacqui Baker, a partner and the head of retail at the consultancy RSM UK, said: “Retail was not a World Cup winner, with many opting to cheer on England from the pub and prioritising their summer getaway, boosting hospitality and travel rather than retail sales.
“Consumers splashed out on fans and food for barbeques due to the heatwave, with many avoiding soaring temperatures on the high street.”

The Brief
Professional golfers competed in triple-digit heat and smoky conditions at the Wildhorse Ladies Golf Classic in Pendleton, adjusting their strategies to manage the challenging environment.
Players made tactical adjustments, including clubbing down because the ball traveled farther in the heat, while prioritizing hydration and nutrition between shots.
Spectators traveled from surrounding areas to watch the tournament, saying the experience gave them newfound appreciation for the athletes' dedication and skill.
PENDLETON, Ore. — Triple-digit heat and thick smoke created an unforgiving test for some of the world's best young golfers at the Wildhorse Ladies Golf Classic. Yet, neither the players nor the fans let the conditions dampen their competitive spirit or enthusiasm.
The tournament brought together 141 golfers competing for valuable points in the Epson Tour's race for the card. Despite temperatures soaring above 100 degrees and visibility reduced by wildfire smoke, players navigated 18 holes with focus and determination.
For golfer Anaka Varma, the key to managing the extreme conditions was straightforward: stick to fundamentals. "Honestly, you just stick to the game plan. And for me, it was pretty simple today. Fairways and greens," Varma said.
Getting an early tee time proved advantageous for Varma, allowing her to play through some of the worst of the smoke and heat. But the environmental conditions created an unexpected challenge—the ball traveled farther in the extreme heat.
"The ball just goes a little further, if anything. So you just club down," Varma explained, noting the adjustment required careful club selection throughout the round.
Playing 18 holes in triple-digit heat demands more than tactical adjustments on the course. Varma emphasized the importance of preparation between shots, particularly hydration and nutrition. "Drink a lot of water, eat a lot of food. Like, you can't be slacking on that for sure. It's more than just playing on the course. It's also hydrating yourself," she said.
While the players managed the challenging conditions, spectators also chose to brave the heat and smoke to watch the professionals compete. Lynn Rodriguez drove from Hermiston to attend the tournament and witness the golfers up close. Walking the course in the extreme heat gave her a deeper appreciation for the athletes' physical and mental endurance.
"You don't get to ride in a car. You have to walk. A lot of these girls are carrying their own bags," Rodriguez said, highlighting the demanding nature of professional golf.
Despite the smoke hanging over the course, Rodriguez said the experience justified the effort. "It just—how they're able to still just compete and play, you know, the best that they can. And they're doing great. It's really impressive," she said.
The Wildhorse Ladies Golf Classic continues through Sunday at Wildhorse Golf Course. For both competitors and fans, the extreme conditions have become just another element that defines the tournament's challenge and showcases the dedication required to excel in professional golf.

ALBANY, Ga. (WALB) — After nearly two weeks of oppressive heat and humidity, SGA is finally getting a break. A more typical summer pattern returns early next week with lower humidity and more comfortable heat index values.
Storms Possible Through Saturday
Tonight, isolated showers and storms remain in the forecast. If storms are slow-moving, they could produce several inches of rain in a short period of time, leading to isolated flash flood concerns in low-lying or poor drainage areas.
Saturday rain chances more confined to our SE counties. Seasonal highs low-mid 90s with heat indices upper 90s to 105. This will be the first day without a Heat Advisory since August 10th.
The Heat Wave Finally Breaks
Sunday and Monday will be the driest days of the next week, with little to no rain expected. This is when the real relief arrives.
Highs in the mid to upper 90s both days, but here’s the key difference — heat indices will only reach the upper 90s to 105 degrees. That’s a significant drop from the dangerous heat indices exceeding 105 that have plagued the area.
What to Expect the Rest of the Week
Rain chances gradually increase through the remainder of next week as the pattern returns to typical summer conditions. Highs will remain in the low to mid 90s with heat indices climbing 102 to 108.
What You Should Do:
- Tonight and Saturday: Keep an eye on the sky for developing storms. Have a way to receive weather alerts and know where to take shelter if strong storms develop.
- Sunday and Monday: This is your window to get outside and enjoy more comfortable conditions. The lower humidity will make it feel much more tolerable.
- Next week: Stay hydrated and continue to take heat precautions, even as conditions improve.

JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - Gardeners are returning home to wilted plants after another hot day, according to Allen Martinson, owner of Martinson’s Garden Works.
Watering advice
Martinson said a quick spray of water will not help wilted plants.
“Won’t do a thing, really do more harm than good. So drink a cup of coffee, take your time, listen to your podcast, do some praying or meditating, whatever it is you do, and let that water soak in. You’ll be doing you and your plants a favor that way,” Martinson said.
He recommends using a soaker hose or drip irrigation when possible to let water soak down to the roots.
Choosing heat-tolerant plants
Martinson said watering is only part of the equation when it comes to caring for plants in extreme heat.
“These are plants that are notoriously better about taking these temperatures that we’re having right now...most of the plants that are blue-green in color are usually heat tolerant plants like a lot of the succulents and a lot of the conifers are very heat tolerant....This is a red yucca. And they bloom beautifully like this all spring long. And they don’t care what the temperatures are. They say, bring it on. They put up their dukes and they take it,” Martinson said.
Martinson suggests holding off on fertilizing or heavy pruning during extreme heat. He recommends using mulch or ground cover plants to keep sun off bare soil and help it hold moisture.
Look to older neighborhoods for clues
Urban horticulturist Felder Rushing said gardeners can identify native, heat-tolerant plants by looking at older parts of town.
“Start looking at plants that you find in the older parts of town, old cemeteries, you know, plants that have been out there for a long time through the winter, through the heavy spring rain, through the heat, through the drought, without any care at all,” Rushing said.
Rushing said traditional expectations for lawns and landscaping may not fit current conditions.
“We were raised thinking big lawns and azaleas were normal. They’re not normal. They’ve always been hard, but the weather changing makes it really rough on it — and us. So stop worrying about it so much,” Rushing said.
Both Martinson and Rushing pointed to lantanas as a heat-tough option that does not require much fuss.

138 transformers and 35 water supply schemes disrupted across state; heavy to very heavy rain likely at isolated places today
As many as 112 roads continue to remain blocked across Himachal Pradesh, while about 138 transformers and 35 water supply schemes also remain disrupted after being damaged due to torrential rains.
As per the State Emergency Operation Centre, of the total blocked roads, 46 are in Mandi, 32 in Kullu, 12 in Chamba, six in Kangra, five each in Shimla, Sirmaur and Una, and one in Lahaul and Spiti.
Similarly, of the total disrupted transformers, 42 are in Mandi, 40 in Sirmaur, 31 in Hamirpur, 21 in Kullu, three in Kangra and one in Shimla.
Additionally, of the total disrupted water supply schemes, 30 are in Hamirpur, four in Shimla and one in Kangra.
Meanwhile, the state is very likely to witness heavy rain on Saturday as the State's Meteorological Centre has issued orange alerts for Shimla, Kangra, Solan, Kullu, Mandi, Una, Bilaspur and Hamirpur districts, with very heavy to heavy rain likely at isolated places throughout the day.
Similarly, yellow weather alerts have been issued for Kinnaur, Sirmaur, Chamba and Lahaul and Spiti, with light to moderate rain likely throughout the day.

Riga: Latvia issued its highest-level weather warning for parts of the country on Friday as a powerful cyclone was forecast to bring torrential rain and strong winds over the weekend, raising the risk of flooding, power outages and transport disruption.
The Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre issued a red warning for heavy rainfall in parts of central Latvia, including areas around Riga and Jelgava.
The warning will run from 8am on Saturday until 1 a.m. on Sunday, though the affected area could change as forecasts are updated, the agency said.
Authorities said the heavy rain could cause widespread flooding of homes, roads, farmland and gardens, with some roads potentially becoming impassable. Electricity and water supplies as well as telecommunications could also be disrupted.
Latvia's State Fire and Rescue Service urged residents to avoid unnecessary trips outdoors, secure loose objects and charge mobile phones in preparation for possible power outages.
Several outdoor events across Latvia have been cancelled because of the forecast.
The storm is also expected to hit neighbouring Estonia, where the environment agency has warned of heavy rain and strong winds over the weekend. Estonian electricity distribution operator Elektrilevi said falling trees and branches could cause power outages, Estonian public broadcaster ERR reported.
